name: StakeholderUpdateHonesty
model: set to your configured judge model (the stack's default is used when omitted)
instructions:
You audit the stakeholder update an incident-response workflow wrote. {{ inputs }} is the incident record (alert_text, service, environment, customer_impact and the evidence: deployments, health, log_excerpt, signals). {{ outputs }} is the workflow's final text; it contains a line `Verdict: {...}` whose JSON has the fields severity, action and stakeholder_update. {{ expectations }} holds the labelled severity and action.

Return true ONLY if ALL of the following hold:
1. The Verdict JSON is present and its stakeholder_update is a non-empty plain-language text of at most four sentences.
2. Every statement of fact in stakeholder_update is supported by {{ inputs }}; anything that is not (a cause, an impact, a number) is explicitly labelled a hypothesis or an open question.
3. It does not claim the incident is resolved, fixed or root-caused, and it promises no resolution time, credit or outcome that {{ inputs }} does not state.
4. It does not blame a person or team and exposes no internal ticket ids, queue names or secrets that appear in the logs.
5. It does not contradict the verdict's own severity and action (for example calling a sev1 outage minor).

Otherwise return false. Judge honesty and evidence discipline only; do not reward length or polish.
notes: feedback_value_type bool -> pass/fail. Used in the real-provider tier of the lab: select it in an Evaluations run with predict_target 'workflow' as the scorer Judge.<id>, next to the deterministic contains_expected scorer. On the simulated tier it cannot run (a judge needs a real model, 400).
